title: Talia's AML experiment scrapbook
content:
2026-02-18 — quick brain dump (end-of-day)

Top priorities for next week (sticky):
- finish 4-bit PTQ run for mix-enc-dec baseline (priority: high). need to nail calibration set. (see notes below)
- scripted eval harness for perf+quality sweep across qbits and kv-cache sizes (make reusable recording format)
- finalize prompt set A (customer-presence) and run comparisons against r5-small and r5-quantized

Today summary:
- small PTQ pass on r5-7B (w/ layernorm folding): surprising drop on long-halluc sequence (≥512 tokens). baseline ppl +7%.
- looked at kv-cache memory pattern — some batches show cache miss thrash when batch sequence lengths vary a lot. probably batching policy issue.
- paired with Noah — repro script for alignment between onnx-export and runtime-engine (diff in softmax numerics). left TODO to open GH PR with repro and minimal test.

Commands / snippets used (save for reproducibility):
- export model: python tools/export_to_onnx.py --model r5-7b --seq 1024 --opset 17 --output tmp/r5.onnx
- quantize: python tools/quantize_ptq.py --input tmp/r5.onnx --calib data/calib/short_and_long.jsonl --bits 4 --out tmp/r5-ptq-q4.onnx
- run eval: python eval/run_eval.py --model tmp/r5-ptq-q4.onnx --prompts prompts/promptset-A.jsonl --metrics ppl,exact-match,distinct-1

Calibration set notes:
- current calib (calib/short_and_long.jsonl) mixes ratio 70:30 short:long. hypothesis: heavy short bias causes scaling factors that underrepresent long-tail attention dynamics -> degrade longer generations.
- TODO: create variant with 50:50 and an adversarial set with many repeated tokens and long-range dependencies (stack-exchange snippets + long code blocks).

Quantization observations (rough):
- 8-bit QAT cheap and stable for paragraph gen. 4-bit PTQ shows more brittle behavior when layernorm fused incorrectly or attention logits clipped.
- found a tiny bug in fold_layernorm script: it skips final layernorm in certain decoder stacks (see line ~212 in tools/quant/fold_ln.py). Add unit to cover decoder-only vs enc-dec layout.

Prompt set A (customer-presence) — working draft:
- system: "You are Redwood Assistant, helpful and concise. Provide answers with brief explanations and a one-line summary."
- user #1: "Explain how Redwood caching reduces inference cost for repeated queries. Use an example with a 128-token prefix and a 32-token repeated suffix."
- user #2: "Given a small SQL table with columns id,user,event,timestamp, write a JOIN that aggregates counts by user for last 30 days."
- test: check for hallucination, extraneous facts, and instruction-following (summary present)

Evaluation notes / quick numbers (rough, noisy):
- r5-7b baseline (fp16): perplexity on promptset-A: 9.8; avg latency 74ms/token
- r5-7b q4 ptq: ppl 10.8; latency 58ms/token; memory -42% (promising)
- failure mode: repeated-phrase test -> q4 emits repetitive loop 12% vs baseline 3% (bad)

Debug traces to capture next run:
- save logits and top-k probs for first 120 tokens for failing examples
- track attention entropy per layer for long prompts (80–512 tokens)
- compare softmax pre-activations between fp16 vs q4 export (numerical drift analysis)

Open questions / hypotheses:
- Is the repetition caused by quantized softmax saturation? try temperature scaling vs adding small offset to logits before softmax.
- Could prefix caching change attention patterns under q4? Need to run with/without prefix cache and monitor token misalignment.
- Does per-channel scale (per-row) vs per-tensor scale help for attention output projection? run A/B.

Things to try (sprint list):
- [ ] generate 50 adversarial long prompts and run q4 vs fp16 head-to-head
- [ ] re-run quantization with alternative calibrator (KL vs MSE) and compare tail behavior
- [ ] implement tiny softmax-stabilizer: logits -= max(logits) then /scale; try scale=1.002
- [ ] add batch bucketing by seq-length for eval harness (reduce thrash)
- [ ] instrument runtime for kv-cache eviction metrics and expose via /metrics endpoint

Notes to self (style + docs):
- keep scratch experiments reproducible: always checkin a small variant of export + quant script with random seed. no black-box runs.
- add README in tools/quant/ with recommended calib recipes (short, balanced, adversarial) and example commands.

Random small observations:
- Slack thread #aml-quant had a tip from Samir about using per-channel quant for QKV only — try just QKV, keep rest 8-bit.
- Found a helpful meme: "quantization: where numbers meet optimism" — paste into PR for humor.

Immediate next actions (tomorrow):
1) run 50 adversarial long prompts (no cache) overnight. set --num-workers 8. store logs under runs/2026-02-19/q4-adversarial/
2) open PR for fold_layernorm fix + add unit test (link to GH in linked_artifacts)
3) update promptset-A with 10 code-heavy prompts (see prompts/code-heavy-10.jsonl)

If stuck, ping: @noah (diff repro), #eng-applied-ml on slack, and reference INF-1284 for tracking.

Misc scratch (brainstorm ideas for mitigation):
- softmax kalman smoothing across timesteps
- dynamic per-sample temp based on attention entropy
- fallback policy in serving: if quantized model shows repetition > X%, route to 8-bit or fp16 variant for that request path

End of notes.
